title: Eef2 loss induces a cortical L2/3 Vgf/Cx3cl1/Son/Ranbp2/Smpd1 state rather than a generic elongation signature
exact_observed_result: Eef2 perturbation produced its largest FDR signature in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut with 575 genes, including Vgf logFC 2.149 and FDR 1.01e-08, Nptx2 logFC 2.946 and FDR 3.02e-08, Cx3cl1 logFC 0.864 and FDR 4.93e-08, and Uchl1 logFC -0.712 and FDR 5.35e-05. Smaller Vgf-positive or Ranbp2-positive signatures appeared in Pvalb, L5 ET, and MB Glut.
biological_interpretation: The mRNA response to Eef2 perturbation is strongly state-gated and biased toward superficial cortical excitatory neurons instead of reading out simple pan-neuronal translation elongation failure.
caveats: The measured Eef2 transcript itself was not FDR-depleted in any tested cell type, so the large downstream response could reflect protein-level editing, unmeasured isoforms, or guide-linked biology not captured by the assayed 3-prime Eef2 row.

prior_expectation.summary: EEF2 is the conserved ribosomal translocation factor and neuronal eEF2 phosphorylation is tied to dendritic mRNA translation; that prior biology predicts translation-related consequences but not this L2/3-centered Vgf/Cx3cl1 abundance state.

citations.supports: neuronal eEF2 phosphorylation and dendritic translation
